boards.title: Claimed by 9am: 10 Study Spots Worth Showing Up Early For
boards.description: Ten documented University of Rochester study environments, spanning quiet reading rooms, collaborative library areas, and reservable project rooms.

cards.title: Great Hall
cards.subtitle: Rush Rhees Library, second floor
cards.notes: Set up at a table in this quiet Rush Rhees space, then use the nearby stairwells for access to the third floor and library offices.
cards.short_summary: A quiet second-floor Rush Rhees study setting with adjacent library services.
cards.evidence_claim: River Campus Libraries describes the Great Hall as a quiet place to study and lists it on the second floor of Rush Rhees Library.
cards.access_notes: Check current Rush Rhees Library hours before visiting.

cards.title: Welles-Brown Room
cards.subtitle: Rush Rhees Library, first floor
cards.notes: Use the room’s comfortable reading-room atmosphere for individual work; it is reached from the Friedlander Lobby opposite Hawkins-Carlson.
cards.short_summary: A plush first-floor room in Rush Rhees with a documented study atmosphere.
cards.evidence_claim: River Campus Libraries says the Welles-Brown Room provides a comfortable club-like atmosphere for study and is accessible from the Friedlander Lobby.
cards.access_notes: The room also hosts speakers, receptions, and social events; confirm availability on arrival.

cards.entity_name: Janis and James S. Gleason Library
cards.title: Gleason Library
cards.subtitle: Rush Rhees Library, first floor
cards.notes: Choose a café-style or counter-height seat for solo work, or move to the open areas when you need a collaborative table.
cards.short_summary: A first-floor Rush Rhees library with individual and collaborative seating.
cards.evidence_claim: Gleason Library offers individual and collaborative study, café-style and counter-height seating, and dedicated quiet spaces.
cards.access_notes: The library states that the space remains open 24 hours during the semester; confirm term-specific access conditions.

cards.title: Gleason Quieter Study Area
cards.subtitle: Inside Gleason Library, Rush Rhees first floor
cards.notes: Head to the designated quieter area when you need a lower-noise setting while remaining close to Gleason’s shared study amenities.
cards.short_summary: A named quieter section within Gleason Library.
cards.evidence_claim: The official Gleason Library page lists a Quieter Study Area among its study options.
cards.access_notes: Located within Gleason Library; follow current building access and library-hour guidance.

cards.title: Gleason Studio 1
cards.subtitle: Gleason Library, Rush Rhees Library
cards.notes: Reserve this four-person studio before a focused team session, and keep the plan within the library’s booking limits for collaborative spaces.
cards.short_summary: A reservable four-person group studio in Gleason Library.
cards.evidence_claim: River Campus Libraries lists Gleason Studio 1 as a reservable space with capacity for four people.
cards.source_title: Reserve a Space | River Campus Libraries
cards.access_notes: University community members may reserve library spaces. Gleason bookings are limited to two hours per day.

cards.title: Carlson Library
cards.subtitle: Computer Studies Building
cards.notes: Pick a quiet-work area for concentration or a collaborative zone for problem sets; public computers and printing are available in the library.
cards.short_summary: A science and engineering library with quiet, collaborative, and technology-supported work areas.
cards.evidence_claim: Carlson Library offers spaces for quiet or collaborative work, plus public computers and printing.
cards.access_notes: Some Carlson rooms require advance reservation through the library booking system; check current library hours.

cards.title: Carlson Room 102
cards.subtitle: Carlson Science and Engineering Library
cards.notes: Book this eight-person room when your group needs a defined work session, and leave time to wrap up before the reservation limit ends.
cards.short_summary: A reservable eight-person project room in Carlson Library.
cards.evidence_claim: River Campus Libraries lists Carlson Library room 102 as a reservable space with capacity for eight people.
cards.source_title: Reserve a Space | River Campus Libraries
cards.access_notes: University community members may reserve library spaces. Carlson bookings are limited to three hours per day.

cards.title: Art & Music Library
cards.subtitle: Rush Rhees Library, ground floor
cards.notes: Use a study table or individual carrel near art and music collections, with public computers, scanners, and viewing stations available nearby.
cards.short_summary: A ground-floor Rush Rhees library with carrels, tables, and media-oriented work tools.
cards.evidence_claim: The Art & Music Library has large study tables, smaller study carrels, viewing stations, scanners, Macs, and PCs.
cards.source_title: Art & Music Library | River Campus Libraries
cards.access_notes: Located on the ground floor of Rush Rhees Library; check the library’s current hours before visiting.

cards.title: Art & Music Library Room 1A
cards.subtitle: Art & Music Library, Rush Rhees Library
cards.notes: Reserve this six-person media-equipped room for collaborative coursework or a viewing assignment, then release it promptly at the end of your slot.
cards.short_summary: A reservable six-person Art & Music Library room for collaborative work or viewing.
cards.evidence_claim: River Campus Libraries lists AM Room 1A as a six-person reservable Art & Music Library space and notes these rooms have specialized gaming and media equipment.
cards.source_title: Reserve a Space | River Campus Libraries
cards.access_notes: University community members may reserve library spaces; booking limits vary by location and are generally two hours per day.

cards.title: iZone Project Room A
cards.subtitle: Barbara J. Burger iZone, Rush Rhees Library ground floor
cards.notes: Reserve this six-person project room for collaborative planning, then pair the session with iZone workshops or peer-led consulting when relevant.
cards.short_summary: A reservable six-person project room in the iZone’s collaborative problem-solving environment.
cards.evidence_claim: River Campus Libraries lists iZone Project Room A as a reservable space with capacity for six people; iZone supports student creative problem-solving through courses, workshops, consulting, and events.
cards.source_title: Reserve a Space | River Campus Libraries
cards.access_notes: University community members may reserve library spaces. iZone bookings are limited to two hours per day.
